ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Loss of trophic hormonal support

An endometrial specimen obtained years after menopause shows fewer and smaller glands without malignant cells. The patient has not received exogenous hormone therapy and has no destructive local inflammatory process. Which change in stimulation most directly explains the adaptation?

  1. Acute arterial occlusion
  2. Reduced estrogenic stimulation
  3. Sustained growth-factor excess
  4. Increased mechanical workload
  5. Chronic epithelial irritation
Answer and explanation

Reduced estrogenic stimulation

Withdrawal of hormonal support reduces tissue activity and promotes atrophy.

Option explanations

Reduced estrogenic stimulation: Withdrawal of hormonal support reduces tissue activity and promotes atrophy.

Sustained growth-factor excess: Growth-factor excess tends to promote proliferation.

Increased mechanical workload: Mechanical workload commonly induces hypertrophy in responsive tissues.

Chronic epithelial irritation: Chronic irritation can produce metaplasia rather than hormonally mediated glandular atrophy.

Acute arterial occlusion: Arterial occlusion causes acute ischemic injury, not the described gradual physiologic change.

Related lecture

Cellular Adaptations (Growth Adaptations): Hypertrophy, Hyperplasia, Atrophy, Metaplasia

References
